title: Differences between Traditional Medicare and Medicare Advantage
source: Dugan K et al. JAMA Network Open. 2025;8(4):e252834 — eAppendix 4
question_text: I keep hearing about Medicare Advantage. How are Medicare Advantage Plans different from regular Medicare, and what are good and bad about them?

accurate_complete: Medicare Advantage: May have lower premiums, deductibles, and cost sharing than traditional Medicare plus a Supplement plan
Medicare Advantage: Has a more restrictive choice of providers and hospitals
Medicare Advantage: You may not be able to keep your doctor
Medicare Advantage: Covers all Medicare Part A and Part B (sometimes Part D) benefits
Medicare Advantage: One must continue to pay the Medicare Part B premium in addition to the Medicare Advantage plan premium
Medicare Advantage: Often offers additional benefits such as vision, hearing, dental, fitness, grocery, OTC card, etc.
Original Medicare: Part A provides coverage for hospital stays (automatic enrollment when applying for Medicare)
Original Medicare: Part B covers doctors' services, outpatient care, and preventive services (optional enrollment)
Original Medicare: Part A has a deductible and some cost sharing but no monthly premium
Original Medicare: Part B has a monthly premium, some cost sharing, and a small deductible
Original Medicare: Premiums and cost sharing can be more expensive than with Medicare Advantage Plans
Original Medicare: Choice of almost any provider, hospital, etc.
Original Medicare: In order to receive coverage for prescription drugs, you must obtain a separate Prescription Drug Plan (Part D)
Original Medicare: Can be paired with a Medigap / Medicare Supplement policy to reduce premiums, deductibles, and cost sharing
accurate_incomplete: Some (but not all) of the Medicare Advantage or Original Medicare topics were substantively covered
not_substantive: None of the Medicare Advantage or Original Medicare topics were substantively discussed
Counselor said they do not know
Otherwise did not substantively answer the question
incorrect: Incorrect information was provided that was substantive enough to materially change the substance of the answer or affect an enrollee's coverage decision

scoring_notes: ALL 14 criteria must be covered to score Accurate and Complete. This is the most demanding rubric in the dataset, which is reflected in the very low baseline (1.5%). Any substantive discussion of both Medicare Advantage AND Original Medicare characteristics that does not cover all 14 points scores as Accurate but Incomplete. The 90.8% Accurate but Incomplete baseline indicates counselors typically give a good answer but cannot cover everything.
